biography:
Thomas Eek Murstad, the pride of Norway, didn't start on a silver spoon. Growing up in a small village nestled amidst the fjords, his first taste of speed came from tinkering with his grandfather's old snowmobile. The roar of the engine, the wind in his hair – it was intoxicating. He transitioned to karting at 14, tearing up local tracks with a raw, untamed talent. Money was tight, forcing him to learn the mechanics of his kart inside and out, a skill that still serves him well today.

His breakthrough came at the Norwegian Karting Championship, where he salvaged a near-impossible victory after a collision on the first lap. Murstad, unfazed, weaved through the pack with breathtaking precision, his kart a blur of controlled chaos. It was this drive, this refusal to give up, that caught the eye of a Kart Cross team manager. 

Since then, Murstad has been a force to be reckoned with in the Kart Cross world. His flashy style and aggressive overtakes have made him a fan favorite, but also earned him a few enemies. Now at 30, considered to be in his peak years, he’s focused on securing that elusive championship title that has so far eluded him, and solidify his place as a motorsport icon.
drivingStyle: Murstad's driving style is best described as a controlled explosion. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and aggressive corner entries, often pushing the limits of his kart and the track. Tire management isn't exactly his forte; he prefers to go all-out, relying on his raw skill to compensate for any loss of grip. Under pressure, he thrives, often pulling off spectacular overtakes in the final laps of a race. He is a gambler, a risk-taker, and the crowd loves him for it.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at the Scandinavian Kart Cross Cup, where Svenson accused Murstad of deliberately taking him out of the race.
A clash of styles and personalities. Petrova, known for her calculated and precise driving, often clashes with Murstad's flamboyant and unpredictable approach.
Alvarez, a veteran of the sport, views Murstad as an upstart challenging the established order, leading to intense on-track battles and off-track sparring.

quirks: Always wears a pair of lucky blue socks inherited from his grandfather during every race.
Listens to a specific Norwegian folk song on repeat right before getting into his kart, claiming it helps him focus.
Has a habit of sketching doodles of his kart on his pit board during breaks, a nervous tic he's had since his early karting days.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. You race to win, or you don't race at all."
careerHighlight: Winning the Norwegian Kart Cross Grand Prix in 2021 after starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical issue in qualifying. He carved his way through the field, showcasing his exceptional overtaking skills and sheer determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the European Kart Cross Championship final in 2022 while leading, costing him a potential championship title. The resulting mechanical damage and his own injuries sidelined him for several weeks.
